gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-anti: Bruno Ace draws every letter with a ruler-straight line and lets each one linger. Zen Kaku Gothic Antique is the opposite talent, a plain sans whose bends flow smoothly and whose t keeps its crossbar and stem matched.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-new: Wide, deliberate, a bit showy: Bruno Ace holds its counters open to the outside and gives each character its own beat. Zen Kaku Gothic New keeps hairlines and swells out entirely.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-zen-maru-gothic: Bruno Ace takes its time, one character per beat. Zen Maru Gothic follows with sans-serif text that never snags on a closed-up bowl, so the eye moves along it like a single thread beneath those drawn-out headlines.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-ibm-plex-sans: IBM Plex Sans reads with a wide channel into every bowl, so the text feels approachable and quick to enter. Bruno Ace is the showpiece, its letterforms bent from one length of tubing, while the body stays low-key.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-zilla-slab: Bruno Ace sets curves as heavy as its stems, like cord, and each counter stays open to the outside. And Zilla Slab, a sturdy slab-serif, brings broad openings on every rounded curve, which is where the pair gets its grip.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-clash-grotesk: Clash Grotesk reads with no thick-and-thin modulation at all, smooth and approachable from line to line. Bruno Ace SC sits above it with letters spread like beads on a long thread, so the two feel loosely strung together.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, a tall-bodied sans-serif whose ascenders look short and whose curve endings keep well apart. Alpino sits snugly beneath Bruno Ace SC's uninterrupted monoline strokes, and the text feels friendly and slightly tight across a page.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-familjen-grotesk: Bruno Ace SC spreads out its open letters like beads on a long thread. Familjen Grotesk, a plain sans with tall lowercase and bowls left unfinished on one side, would sit well at a modest size beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-hind: Hind reads steadily, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals and the ends of its c never turning inward. Bruno Ace SC is the show-off with its straight-edged, constant strokes, while Hind does the quiet work.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-fs-nunito: Bruno Ace SC spreads its open letters like beads on a thread, with hairlines that never appear anywhere. Nunito, a plain sans with big round lowercase bowls, softens it underneath.
